## Merge-risk assessment

**Risk: medium. Recommendation: Validate before merge. 🟢 High confidence.** This assessment covers [sonic-mgmt PR #29453](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/29453) at [head `975020b37449c1f15fc044610f7b47b434ab2fe3`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/975020b37449c1f15fc044610f7b47b434ab2fe3), against [base `master` `088fcee916f8bd65dcc3870859d0040c860adf84`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/088fcee916f8bd65dcc3870859d0040c860adf84), at the `2026-11-22T00:05:49.060Z` cutoff.

### Why this is medium risk

- The 18-line selection change adds module-prefix skips for `crm/test_crm.py`, `ip/test_ip_packet.py`, and `ssh/test_ssh_stress.py` when [issue #29438](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/29438) is open and the lane is VPP `t0`. Prefix matching suppresses every parameterized case in each module; with [PR #29439](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/29439), the same issue now gates 12 modules on this lane.
- A retained [exact-base `t0-vpp` plan](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/publictestplan/6b01c3871c0f51380a2e9908) recorded source `088fcee…`: CRM failed the same nexthop-counter check on attempts 0/1/2; IP packet forwarding failed first and passed retry 1; SSH stress errored in teardown because route consistency did not recover, then passed retry 1.
- In the fixed 14-day VPP `t0` KVM lane, outcomes worsened sharply after November 15: CRM first/final pass rates fell from 99.5%/99.8% to 58.6%/74.2%; IP from 99.8%/100% to 85.0%/90.5%; SSH from 99.3%/99.6% to 88.0%/95.0%. This corroborates instability, but does not independently prove host CPU oversubscription as the cause.
- No product code, assertion, retry count, xfail, or new LogAnalyzer suppression changes. Retained VPP `t0` plans in the window were KVM-only, and other VPP topologies are outside the condition. Static and conditional-mark checks completed successfully.

### Validation gap

The [exact-head `t0-vpp` check](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/runs/137023195547) was still running at the cutoff, so there is no completed revision-matched runtime result. Before merge, verify all three modules are skipped only on `t0-vpp`, remain selected on `t1-lag-vpp`/dualtor VPP lanes, and retain non-blocking visibility until the root cause is fixed. Also note that issue-state lookup fails open: an API failure leaves these skips active even after the issue is closed.

MERGE_RISK=medium

## Merge-risk assessment

**Risk: medium. Recommendation: Validate before merge. 🟢 High confidence.** This assessment covers [sonic-mgmt PR #29439](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/29439) at [head `39bdf3768343bb406b823545cc3b4c182c8a5c88`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/39bdf3768343bb406b823545cc3b4c182c8a5c88), against [base `master` `1b7d6c9c8247383a7b123dc1132d23c0debadbd2`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/1b7d6c9c8247383a7b123dc1132d23c0debadbd2), at the `2026-11-20T21:04:16Z` assessment cutoff.

### What changed

- The one-file change in [`tests_mark_conditions_sonic_vpp.yaml`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/39bdf3768343bb406b823545cc3b4c182c8a5c88/tests/common/plugins/conditional_mark/tests_mark_conditions_sonic_vpp.yaml) adds nine module-level skips for the KVM VPP `t0` lane, covering ARP, Everflow, FDB, loopback, route-performance, and SRv6 modules.
- Every entry requires the open tracking [issue #29438](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/29438), `asic_type == vpp`, and `topo_name == t0`. No product code, shared fixture, retry, xfail, or log-analyzer suppression changed; other VPP topologies remain selected by the condition.
- The open issue documents the same t0-vpp instability and the intended temporary scope. Direct inspection of the conditional-mark plugin confirms module-prefix matching and issue-conditioned evaluation.

### Evidence and gaps

- Static validation checks, including the conditional-mark validation path, completed successfully; qualified approval is present for the changed folder.
- Retained target-branch t0-vpp history shows matching setup/teardown, port-readiness, CPU-readiness, MAC-move, and route-installation failures in the affected modules. This corroborates the bounded mitigation but does not independently prove CPU oversubscription as the root cause.
- The exact-head impacted-area runtime jobs, including [t0-vpp](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/runs/136566003797), were still in progress at the fixed cutoff; no completed exact-head plan/result is included in this assessment. Before merge, verify the nine modules are skipped only on t0-vpp, that t1-lag-vpp/dualtor-vpp continue to execute them, and that the skips are removed or no longer active after issue #29438 closes.

MERGE_RISK=medium

- **Revision:** [`eaf97d2069453ac163ed9636e2276d494c14809c`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/eaf97d2069453ac163ed9636e2276d494c14809c) against base [`ec32c9c76461cda00032951919c0b37df1c8442f`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/ec32c9c76461cda00032951919c0b37df1c8442f). [Build 1281337](https://dev.azure.com/mssonic/be1b070f-be15-4154-aade-b1d3bfb17054/_build/results?buildId=1281337) exercised merge commit [`0f42fccf6e29badcba4e7a36815e8078a4c8fe9b`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/0f42fccf6e29badcba4e7a36815e8078a4c8fe9b), which contains both revisions.
- **Scope:** One test replaces the hard-coded 180-second SSH-drop wait with the existing shared 300-second warm-reboot timeout ([changed call](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/eaf97d2069453ac163ed9636e2276d494c14809c/tests/gnmi/test_gnoi_system_reboot.py#L130-L136), [shared value](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/eaf97d2069453ac163ed9636e2276d494c14809c/tests/common/reboot.py#L78-L80)). Recovery assertions remain intact; the PR adds no skip/xfail, retry, selection change, fixture/plugin change, or log-analyzer suppression.
- **Observed validation:** The exact tested merge passed the affected case first attempt in the [`t0` plan](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6aff004ba664af5da815d6dc) (`1/1`, no retry); its log used `timeout=300` and observed SSH absent after 48 seconds. In clean 14-day `master` BaselineTest controls, standard `t0` was `208/208` first/final pass while cSONiC `t0` was `41/43`; both failures had `Exception: DUT vlab-01 did not shutdown`.

That supports a too-short test threshold rather than a rejected reboot.
- **Remaining validation:** At cutoff `2026-11-19T17:14:47.716Z`, the PR's cSONiC check had not produced an independently queryable affected-case result. Confirm that lane on this head (or retain the PR's targeted same-image evidence) before merge; other required checks and branch protection still apply.

## Merge-risk assessment

**Medium merge risk — Validate before merge** for head [`6ffb8fc`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/6ffb8fccc591f9845dbc792fe3acb3fc331e8bb3) against base [`1dfff00`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/1dfff00b994b7c47e1fcb3ac6caa1632c4b13ba2).

**Confidence:** 🟢 High — the exact three-file diff, caller/cleanup paths, revision-matched CI provenance, retained testcase results, and module logs agree; remaining uncertainty is limited to untested physical multi-ASIC behavior and the no-`psutil` `top` fallback.

### Why medium

- This changes a shared eBGP shutdown/startup readiness helper used by Everflow and SFP suites, so failures can affect module setup/teardown and leave BGP recovery work to the fixture cleanup path. The change is bounded and fail-closed: it preserves the 10% threshold, five samples, route checks, retry budgets, and cleanup; missing samples or missing `orchagent` readings now reject readiness.
- No assertion weakening, broader skip/xfail, retry increase, or log-analyzer suppression was added. The one-line `monit_process` change only widens the existing `top` fallback to retain full process names.

### Revision-matched validation

- Azure CI tested merge commit [`7582dd4`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/7582dd4830d56fc29921c403e4e964ce70716632), which merges the assessed head into the recorded base.
- The [`t0-vpp` plan](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6af5e531e569af8ba6c1e1bb) and [`t1-lag-vpp` plan](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6af5e62222b9aac341f5de69) each passed all 96 applicable `everflow/test_everflow_ipv6.py` cases with four expected skips and no retries. Logs show a 49.8% CPU window was rejected, followed by acceptance only after five complete low-CPU samples.
- Across affected Everflow/SFP rows, 408/408 executed first attempts passed; 1,163 rows skipped and two xfail-skipped. Six `sfputil` cases executed successfully on `t0`/`t1-lag`; chassis and SFP API variants did not execute. Direct `monit_process` CPU/memory checks also passed on `t0`, `t1-lag`, and `t2`.
- The historical same-source/image pair corroborates the intended defect: the [failing plan](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6af446b739cc27878b92f002) passed 95/96 applicable cases and errored only in final eBGP teardown at the old CPU gate, while its [companion plan](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6af446b522b9aac341f5db65) passed 96/96.

### Remaining validation

Before merge, run the assessed head on one physical multi-ASIC DUT through an Everflow or SFP path that actually invokes shutdown and restoration, and explicitly exercise the no-`psutil` `top -w 512` fallback. Confirm every orchagent instance is sampled, high CPU remains rejected, and BGP is restored after both success and forced failure.

The optional cSONiC job failed during topology preparation with zero tests; several other retained CI failures were in unrelated CoPP, SRv6, VLAN, BGP-reload, and dualtor cases rather than this helper.

Assessed [sonic-mgmt PR #29131](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/29131) at [head `a1a1634d5ad429c565821f51a418773fa1b21157`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/a1a1634d5ad429c565821f51a418773fa1b21157) against [base `05e879347ba14a1e7d165e4cc6f8f1dac43646a2`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/05e879347ba14a1e7d165e4cc6f8f1dac43646a2) on [`master`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/tree/master). The PR is now merged; this remains an evidence-backed assessment of the pinned revision, not a merge or approval action.

### Scope and findings

- The six-file change is confined to `tests/acl/test_acl.py` and five ACL rule templates. It removes the fixed t0 VLAN-name restriction, derives three usable addresses per nonlegacy VLAN subnet, passes VLAN-specific second-VLAN destinations into the templates, and restores the four temporary template variables after the module fixture yields. No production code, CI selection, assertion weakening, retry/xfail, or LogAnalyzer suppression was added.
- The shared `acltb_test_rules.j2` template is also rendered by [`tests/ssh/test_ssh_stress.py`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/a1a1634d5ad429c565821f51a418773fa1b21157/tests/ssh/test_ssh_stress.py#L114-L121) and [`tests/show_techsupport/test_techsupport.py`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/a1a1634d5ad429c565821f51a418773fa1b21157/tests/show_techsupport/test_techsupport.py#L77-L83). The Jinja defaults preserve their legacy output when the new variables are absent, and normal fixture teardown restores state.
- Residual code risk: the new `extra_vars.update(...)` occurs before the fixture yields at [`test_acl.py` lines 446-449](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/a1a1634d5ad429c565821f51a418773fa1b21157/tests/acl/test_acl.py#L446-L449), while cleanup is only after the yield at [lines 662-667](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/a1a1634d5ad429c565821f51a418773fa1b21157/tests/acl/test_acl.py#L662-L667). An exception during later fixture setup can therefore bypass cleanup and leave session-scoped template variables for consumers such as SSH stress or techsupport. A finalizer or `try/finally` around the state mutation would close this gap.

### Validation evidence

- [Azure build `1275729`](https://dev.azure.com/mssonic/be1b070f-be15-4154-aade-b1d3bfb17054/_build/results?buildId=1275729) tested source version [`ed6ec501e0a6acb6a258f516c1a1646e330c263b`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/ed6ec501e0a6acb6a258f516c1a1646e330c263b), whose merge commit includes the assessed head. The revision-matched PR plans were finished; the relevant [`t0` plan](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6af759e2f254454a18bf01aa) and [optional cSONiC t0 plan](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6af759e2889b518305773347) each recorded 384/1000 first-attempt successes, 616 skips, and zero failures/errors/retries for `acl/test_acl.py`. Across seven impacted-area plans, the changed module had no failed/error/retry rows.
- Six comparable [`master` t0 baseline plans](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6af7393b889b51830577331e) through [the final baseline plan](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6af793fb3d45574e9f1154bf), using the same KVM/VS/Force10-S6000 lane and image `SONiC.master.1275060-1bf756f7b`, recorded 2304/6000 first-attempt successes, 3696 skips, and zero failures/errors/retries. The candidate t0 lane has the same 38.4% success / 61.6% skip distribution.
- The current PR t0 plans parameterized only `Vlan1000`; they did not exercise the new nonlegacy/two-VLAN or IPv6-only derived-address path. The final `two_vlan_a` result of 8 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed on a physical t0 testbed is author-reported in [the PR comment](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/29131#issuecomment-6865633333), not independently verified by this assessment. A retained baseline `two_vlan_a` plan [did not select `acl/test_acl.py`](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6af793961bc7a99e1f8c02ab).

### Remaining validation

Run the focused `acl/test_acl.py` sequence with `two_vlan_a` and a nonlegacy VLAN, including the isolated-v6 t0 case, and verify that a forced setup failure cannot leave `vlan2_*` values in the shared variable manager. Treat these as post-merge follow-ups because the PR merged during assessment.

- **sonic-utilities#4384 and #4898:** at #4384's head, `pfcwd start` has no `POLL_INTERVAL` check in either mode, and the two PRs conflict exactly there. The plan expects the rebase to skip the check in hardware mode, since the CLI cannot change `POLL_INTERVAL` there. Case 4 has this.
- **L245, reboot types:** yes. Case 10 now runs the refusal for `warm-reboot`, `fast-reboot` and `express-reboot`, since a refused reboot costs nothing. The storm during the reboot stays `warm-reboot` only. I also added that without #4854 the check sees no stormed queue in hardware mode, so the reboot goes ahead.
- **L259, case 11:** the platform's detection window for each port's own detection time. Case 11 now says so, and the table lists case 11.
- **L285, a `failed` port:** clearing the port's `pfcwd_sw_enable` before the start. orchagent then writes `failed` (case 7). Case 15 says so.

These cover FLEX_COUNTER_DB, `BIG_RED_SWITCH_MODE` in COUNTERS_DB with traffic dropped, a missed storm while the poll is off, the history fields, and the stormed but undropped queue for `alert`. Case 9 now starts `alert` on a port that is the only one configured, since with another port on another action #4384 refuses it as an action mismatch.
- **L173, a software row without `restoration_time`:** confirmed. orchagent writes an empty `PFC_WD_RESTORATION_TIME`, and `pfc_restore.lua` skips the queue. @az-pz Thanks for the review and for approving. I pushed d8601d188 after your review, so GitHub dismissed the approval. The replies to your five comments are in their threads, and 2826668c3 updates lines 128-130 for the question below.

> Line 128: the file is keyed by SAI configuration where it matters. Which SAI property selects the recovery model, and does the suite read it from the SAI configuration files on the DUT?

In the SAI that sonic-buildimage ships today, no property selects it. The Broadcom XGS SAI 15.2.1.0.0.0.50.1 and DNX SAI 15.2.1.0.0.0.11.3 have no setting for it and use timer recovery, the model the SAI defines. The Broadcom XGS SDK also has a PFC-state recovery mode, which ends recovery when the pause stops (line 91). A SAI build can select it, either by default or through its configuration file.

The model matters only for the hardware watchdog. In software mode on every platform, and in hybrid DLR mode, orchagent's restore script (`pfc_restore.lua`, or `pfc_restore_cisco-8000.lua`) ends recovery `restoration_time` after the pause stops.

No, the suite does not read the SAI configuration file for these values. No SAI attribute or STATE_DB field reports the model, and a setting in the file has no effect on a SAI build that does not know it. So an entry is keyed by HWSKU and, where a value depends on it, by the version of the vendor SAI package in the syncd container. A DUT whose version has no entry skips the case, and the skip message names the missing entry. Lines 128 and 130 now say this, and lines 91 and 93 match. The same key covers the detection window, whose step a SAI setting can change.

### Startup prerequisite reproduced; reset-only recovery

The failure is before server-down injection, not a failure of the injected server-outage scenario.

The original buildimage CI worker ran the faulty-Y-cable module, ARP extended, and then `test_server_down[active-standby]`. Upper PMON was recreated immediately before the ICMP responder stopped. The next responder fixture increased the heartbeat interval from 100ms to 3000ms but did not clear accumulated suspension. All 24 upper ports stayed active/unhealthy and all 24 lower ports standby/unhealthy through three attempts on that worker.

A faithful predecessor replay captured the real exponential suspension path: 0.8, 1.6, 3.2, 6.4, 12.8, 25.6, and repeated 51.2-second windows. It narrowly passed when the old timer expired inside the health gate; that pass was not treated as a fix.

The phase-aligned warm-PMON [control](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6aebce8a0a7ed00efb0152f0), pinned to diagnostic `f3df9e43647d08de4e38c460da0f7badacda84bd`, then reproduced the exact original assertion on the same `SONiC.master-30444.1266929-476cba3a4` image:

> mux_cable status is unexpected. Should be (active, healthy). Test can't proceed.

Both ToRs retained the original all-24-port unhealthy signature after responder startup. Only `config muxcable reset-heartbeat-suspend all` was applied at the counterfactual boundary. All ports became healthy, with unchanged linkmgrd, TeamMgr, TeamSync and PMON PIDs, unchanged mux roles, and `interval_v4=3000` preserved. The selected-server PTF capture received no probes during the failed health window; request/reply traffic returned after the reset. Pretest, the diagnostic and posttest all passed.

The precise timer duration on the historical worker was not logged. The controlled run proves the reconstructed suspension mechanism and the narrow recovery; it does not retroactively measure that lost timer. The successful CI retry used a fresh worker and different predecessors, so it was not an unchanged stateful replay of this precursor.

Thanks, adding the plain-minigraph baseline matches #28736 and fixes the BGP_GLOBALS drift. One concern about also removing GOLDEN_OVERRRIDDEN_TABLES:

1. LT2/FT2: FEATURE and PORT were added in #22696 because on LT2/FT2, an empty golden override differs from a plain minigraph load (FEATURE is missing BMP, PORT is missing "fec": "rs"). That comparison was already against a plain minigraph baseline back then, so removing them likely brings the failure back. Was this run on an LT2/FT2 testbed?

2. MACsec: config_reload() always passes -o when --enable_macsec is set, so the "plain" baseline still includes the deployed MACSEC_PROFILE, while the empty override removes it. MACSEC_PROFILE in the list was what kept MACsec runs passing.

3. Coverage: the single-ASIC test is currently skipped in CI (#25931 / vs t2), and the UT2 validation covers the single-ASIC file only. The multi-ASIC file's list removal is covered only by the vs t2 checker, without MACsec.

Suggestion: keep the new baseline reload, and keep a reduced exemption list (at least FEATURE, PORT, MACSEC_PROFILE), unless LT2/FT2 and MACsec runs show they're no longer needed.

If the LT2/FT2 and MACsec runs are passing without the list, the changes lgtm.

## Merge-risk assessment

Assessed [sonic-mgmt PR #28977](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/28977) at [head `c1db4f7c27a5ac49cb1a09732ced2ce11ad1dce7`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/c1db4f7c27a5ac49cb1a09732ced2ce11ad1dce7) against `master` base `b7ef1b4060ca6bf52b025eea68960678323536ea`.

- **Risk: medium.** The change is confined to HFT test infrastructure, but shared fixtures now stop/recreate the standalone `hft` container, clear HFT profiles and sessions, manage the PTF InfluxDB process, restart OTEL/systemd services, and can exercise a mapped port shutdown. A partial setup or cleanup failure can affect reserved DUT/PTF state.
- **Recommendation: Validate before merge** (this assessment completed after the PR was merged). The [PR description](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/28977) reports physical single-ASIC SN5640 validation and fixture-unit coverage; public CI checks, including [Azure.sonic-mgmt](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/runs/138133765974), are green for the main lane.
- The dependency behavior is consistent with [sonic-buildimage#30211](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/30211), which moves `countersyncd` into the disabled-by-default standalone `hft` feature. The changed [HFT test plan](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/c1db4f7c27a5ac49cb1a09732ced2ce11ad1dce7/docs/testplan/HFT-test-plan.md) documents the required single-ASIC reservation, direct container launch, and recovery path.
- Remaining validation is an installed-image, standalone-HFT run covering setup failure, interrupted-run recovery, OTEL/HFT restoration, active-session cleanup, and the full PTF dataplane path across supported hardware; the available KVM HFT executions were capability-skipped and do not prove this path.

> Thanks, this is careful work. I read the setup and the limit calculation in `test_ssh_stress.py`, and the cleanup in `ssh_stress_command.py`.
> 
> **What works well**
> 
> * **Limits from this DUT's own serial baselines** (`_derive_stress_requirements`): each command's limit adds up the slowest command of every pair plus a margin, the cycle count comes from the time one round needs, and p95 is checked instead of every single completion. That's a sound replacement for the old 3 × baseline + 1 s rule.
> * **Strict restore checks:** stale stress state, including VRF-qualified keys, is checked before the run starts; the PortChannels are checked through `teamdctl`; and on VPP, `route_check`/monit must recover.
> * **Commands on the DUT are cleaned up properly:** each runs in its own `setsid` process group with SIGTERM/SIGKILL fencing, `done.json` is published only once the group is shown to be gone, and the recorded PID is used if the wrapper has died. This stops a stress command from changing the DUT after the test has restored it.
> * The parent head passed 100/100 runs, and this head passed canaries on both topologies.
> 
> **Points to address**
> 
> 1. **The unit-test file isn't run in CI** (inline). No CI job runs `tests/ssh/unit_tests/`.
> 2. **Self-calibrated limits** (inline): a slowdown that affects every command can't be caught.
> 3. **Cycle floor:** with `MIN_STRESS_CYCLES = 3`, a slow DUT gets about 15 samples per command, so "p95" is effectively the maximum. Please log the cycle count and sample count, and consider failing or skipping with a reason when the derived count is at the floor.
> 4. **Size:** the test grew from 473 to 1,381 lines, plus a 442-line remote helper, for a test that only runs on two VPP topologies. A short design note at the top of `ssh_stress_command.py` would help future maintainers: the `owner.json`/`done.json` protocol, how fencing works, and the PID fallback.
> 
> **Smaller points**
> 
> * Copilot's last summary mentions descendants escaping the process-group fence. That only happens if a command calls `setsid` or double-forks, and none of the stress commands do. A comment stating that assumption would close the question.
> * CodeQL: `previous_term` and `previous_int` may be uninitialized (`ssh_stress_command.py:350,352`), and there are empty `except` blocks at `:137` and `:181`. Please fix them or add a comment explaining why they're safe.
> * Worst-case teardown is `THREAD_JOIN_TIMEOUT` = 410 s on top of the 5-minute stress run. Worth stating in the test plan, since it counts against PR-checker time.

1. The unit tests cover the new code and have been useful in finding bugs. Adding them to CI is additional infrastructure work that I will defer to a follow-up PR.
2. This test is meant to test concurrency degradation, not serial performance. Unless we have an agreed-upon VPP SLO, it is not reasonable to add arbitrary ceilings for areas that this test is not meant to address.
3. Completed and required cycle counts are already logged, as are per-command sample counts. At the three-cycle floor, the p95 is effectively the maximum, which makes the test stricter, not weaker.
4. The request for additional documentation is reasonable. Since this PR is already large and fully validated, I will defer this documentation request to a follow-up PR.
5. The five commands are controlled, and none calls `setsid` or double-forks. This is not an exploitable path for the workload being tested.
6. `previous_term` and `previous_int` are initialized to `None` before the try. The `ProcessLookupError` handlers are deliberate process-exit races and have comments. Also, CodeQL passed.
7. 410s is a worst-case failure-path join budget, not unconditional teardown time.

### Physical-device reproduction: 30-second deadline and 60-second retry

Executed `gnmi/test_gnmi_stress.py::test_gnmi_latency_01` on a **Nokia-7215 (ARMHF), mx topology, SONiC 20260510.22** on October 27, 2026.

A separate diagnostic variant ran **20 down/up iterations (40 logical Set operations)** on the same DUT, image, TLS fixture and channel. Each operation first used a 30-second deadline. Only `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` triggered one new request with the identical payload and a 60-second deadline. Individual attempts were measured with a client-side monotonic clock.

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| Original 30-second attempts | **40/40 `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`**, elapsed 30.001754–30.003375 s |
| New requests with a 60-second deadline | **40/40 successful**, elapsed **22.953417–36.401577 s** |
| Retry mean / median | **30.591551 / 30.562824 s** |
| Successful retries taking more than 30 seconds | **26/40** |
| First attempt + retry total per logical operation | 52.956952–66.404564 s, including logging/retry overhead |

For example, the first down operation timed out after **30.002569 s**; its new 60-second retry succeeded after **30.601678 s**, for **60.604674 s** total.

All 20 iterations completed. The diagnostic test deliberately re-raised the first 30-second timeout afterward to preserve the reproduction: **1 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped**, pytest runtime **2731.945 s**. The test plan also ended FAILED. Configuration rollback, critical-process health verification and certificate cleanup completed; the plan released its testbed reservation.

**Interpretation and limits:** This reproduces the 30-second deadline failure and demonstrates successful retries within a 60-second budget on this device/image. A retry is a **new RPC**, not an extension of the timed-out RPC; these measurements do not establish when the original server-side work completed. Outstanding work and repeating the same update can affect retry timing. This was an instrumented release-aligned diagnostic variant, **not an execution of this PR's unchanged two-line patch** at `ccc8c522531965f8c491403c5ef20d58497a597b`, and not a clean 60-second-only qualification run. It does not establish that the underlying server latency is fixed.

The physical-run logs and per-attempt measurements are retained internally; no public physical-test log URL is available. The PR's source diff remains limited to the two deadline changes.

This directly addresses the [reported E2BIG failure at about 900 neighbors](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/27503).
- The helper is shared by [traffic-shift tests](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/3d96f3a19e8f4596a14b444a70f27780301bc445/tests/bgp/test_traffic_shift.py#L239-L265) and the [line-card suite](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/3d96f3a19e8f4596a14b444a70f27780301bc445/tests/bgp/test_traffic_shift_lc.py#L230-L265), where restoration runs during teardown and restarts BGP. A command or stdin incompatibility can therefore leave neighbors absent or BGP unhealthy; this bounded shared-helper/recovery blast radius supports `medium`, not `low`.

Just wanted to provide some context: this is purely a control plane issue, so physical hardware testing is likely not necessary.

The JSON exceeds Linux’s per-argument limit, so the command fails before it can update ConfigDB. This PR passes the same data through stdin instead, avoiding that limit and successfully updating ConfigDB. The issue is not related to the data plane or any hardware specific code paths.

I validated this on single-ASIC and 4-ASIC SONiC VS images from current master: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/93f8290638bb838004aaf27c918c44bf98efa607

<details>
<summary>Logs & Replication Steps</summary>

**Old implementation**

```text
================ OLD ================
$ sudo sonic-cfggen  -a '<BGP_NEIGHBOR JSON>' --write-to-db
Payload:  926 entries, 147387 bytes inline in the command (limit: 131072 bytes per argument)
Result:   rc=7 (E2BIG), Error executing command.
ConfigDB: 0 BGP_NEIGHBOR keys
```

**PR implementation**

```text
================ NEW ================
$ sudo sonic-cfggen  -j /dev/stdin --write-to-db
Payload:  926 entries, 147387 bytes on stdin
Result:   rc=0
ConfigDB: 926 BGP_NEIGHBOR keys

ConfigDB BGP_NEIGHBOR == input JSON: True (926/926 entries)
Restored: full ConfigDB == pre-test snapshot: True
```

**Reproduction script**

It loads `restore_bgp_neighbors()` from the [parent commit](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/c6fdcbca708f26865c52ee197c3c5d7a230c5c3e) and from the [PR head](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/3d96f3a19e8f4596a14b444a70f27780301bc445), and runs both on a live DUT through sonic-mgmt's `MultiAsicSonicHost`.

```python3
import ast
import errno
import inspect
import ipaddress
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess

import tests.bgp.bgp_helpers as bgp_helpers
from tests.common.devices.multi_asic import MultiAsicSonicHost
from tests.common.errors import RunAnsibleModuleFail
from tests.common.helpers.bgp import get_asic_namespace, get_db_cli_prefix, namespace_cli_arg
from tests.common.plugins.ansible_fixtures import ansible_adhoc  # noqa: F401 (sonic-mgmt's fixture)
from tests.common.utilities import wait_until

OLD_SHA = "c6fdcbca708f26865c52ee197c3c5d7a230c5c3e"  # parent of the PR head
NEW_SHA = "3d96f3a19e8f4596a14b444a70f27780301bc445"  # PR head
COUNT = 926
SONIC_MGMT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(bgp_helpers.__file__)))

PROBE = """import os, errno
m = 32 * os.sysconf('SC_PAGE_SIZE')
def run(n):
    pid = os.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        try:
            os.execv('/bin/true', ['/bin/true', 'x' * n])
        except OSError as e:
            os._exit(100 + e.errno)
    return os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(os.waitpid(pid, 0)[1])
print('PAGE_SIZE=%d MAX_ARG_STRLEN=%d' % (m // 32, m))
print('execv argv[1] of %d bytes incl. NUL: exit=%d' % (m, run(m - 1)))
print('execv argv[1] of %d bytes incl. NUL: exit=%d (100+E2BIG=%d)' % (m + 1, run(m), 100 + errno.E2BIG))
"""


def load_restore(sha):
    src = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", SONIC_MGMT, "show", sha + ":tests/bgp/bgp_helpers.py"], text=True)
    node = next(n for n in ast.parse(src).body
                if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "restore_bgp_neighbors")
    fsrc = ast.get_source_segment(src, node)
    glb = dict(bgp_helpers.__dict__)
    exec(compile(fsrc, sha[:12] + ":tests/bgp/bgp_helpers.py", "exec"), glb)
    return glb["restore_bgp_neighbors"], fsrc


class ShellRecorder(object):
    def __init__(self, host):
        self._host, self.calls = host, []

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        return getattr(self._host, name)

    def shell(self, cmd, *args, **kwargs):
        call = {"cmd": cmd, "stdin": kwargs.get("stdin")}
        self.calls.append(call)
        try:
            res = self._host.shell(cmd, *args, **kwargs)
        except RunAnsibleModuleFail as exc:
            call["rc"], call["msg"] = exc.results.get("rc"), exc.results.get("msg")
            raise
        call["rc"] = res["rc"]
        return res


def read_neighbors(dut, nsarg):
    return json.loads(dut.command("sudo sonic-cfggen {} -d --var-json BGP_NEIGHBOR".format(nsarg))["stdout"] or "{}")


def read_configdb(dut, nsarg):
    return json.loads(dut.shell("sudo sonic-cfggen {} -d --print-data".format(nsarg))["stdout"])


def count_keys(dut, db_cli):
    out = dut.shell("sudo {} CONFIG_DB keys 'BGP_NEIGHBOR|*' | grep -c . || true".format(db_cli))["stdout"]
    return int(out.strip() or 0)


def build_scale_table(original, total):
    """Clone the DUT's own entries, changing only the peer address key and `name`."""
    table = {k: dict(v) for k, v in original.items()}
    ip = ipaddress.ip_address
    sources = sorted(original.items(), key=lambda kv: (ip(kv[0]).version, ip(kv[0])))
    bases = {4: int(ip("10.200.0.0")), 6: int(ip("fc00:200::"))}
    i = 0
    while len(table) < total:
        key, val = sources[i % len(sources)]
        new_key = str(ip(bases[ip(key).version] + 2 * i + 1))
        assert new_key not in table
        entry = dict(val)
        if "name" in entry:
            entry["name"] = "{}-{:04d}".format(val["name"], i + 1)
        table[new_key] = entry
        i += 1
    return table


def test_pr28707_restore_bgp_neighbors(ansible_adhoc, request):  # noqa: F811
    duthost = MultiAsicSonicHost(ansible_adhoc, request.config.getoption("--ansible-host-pattern"), None, "t1")

    head = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", SONIC_MGMT, "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip()
    assert head == NEW_SHA, "sonic-mgmt on PYTHONPATH is at {}, expected {}".format(head, NEW_SHA)
    old_restore, old_src = load_restore(OLD_SHA)
    new_restore, new_src = load_restore(NEW_SHA)
    assert new_src == inspect.getsource(bgp_helpers.restore_bgp_neighbors).rstrip("\n")
    assert "-a '{}'" in old_src and "-j /dev/stdin" in new_src

    probe = duthost.shell("python3 -", stdin=PROBE)["stdout"]
    max_arg_strlen = int(re.search(r"MAX_ARG_STRLEN=(\d+)", probe).group(1))
    assert "{} bytes incl. NUL: exit=0".format(max_arg_strlen) in probe
    assert "{} bytes incl. NUL: exit={} ".format(max_arg_strlen + 1, 100 + errno.E2BIG) in probe

    for asic_index in duthost.get_frontend_asic_ids():
        ns = get_asic_namespace(duthost, asic_index)
        nsarg, db_cli, tag = namespace_cli_arg(ns), get_db_cli_prefix(duthost, asic_index), ns or "default"
        label = " ({})".format(ns) if ns else ""
        snap_path, scale_path = "/tmp/pr28707-snapshot-{}.json".format(tag), "/tmp/pr28707-scale-{}.json".format(tag)

        pre_full = read_configdb(duthost, nsarg)
        original = pre_full.get("BGP_NEIGHBOR", {})
        assert original, "no BGP_NEIGHBOR entries to clone"
        duthost.copy(content=json.dumps({"BGP_NEIGHBOR": original}), dest=snap_path)
        scale = build_scale_table(original, COUNT)
        try:
            duthost.copy(content=json.dumps({"BGP_NEIGHBOR": scale}), dest=scale_path)
            duthost.shell("sudo sonic-cfggen {} -j {} --write-to-db".format(nsarg, scale_path))
            assert read_neighbors(duthost, nsarg) == scale

            removed = bgp_helpers.remove_bgp_neighbors(duthost, asic_index)
            assert removed == scale and count_keys(duthost, db_cli) == 0
            payload = json.dumps({"BGP_NEIGHBOR": removed})
            assert len(payload.encode()) + 1 > max_arg_strlen

            old = ShellRecorder(duthost)
            try:
                old_restore(old, asic_index, removed)
                raise AssertionError("old restore_bgp_neighbors() unexpectedly succeeded")
            except RunAnsibleModuleFail:
                pass
            call, old_keys = old.calls[0], count_keys(duthost, db_cli)
            print("\n================ OLD{} ================".format(label))
            print("$ " + call["cmd"].replace(payload, "<BGP_NEIGHBOR JSON>"))
            print("Payload:  {} entries, {} bytes inline in the command (limit: {} bytes per argument)".format(
                len(removed), len(payload.encode()), max_arg_strlen))
            print("Result:   rc={} ({}), {}".format(call["rc"], errno.errorcode.get(call["rc"]), call["msg"]))
            print("ConfigDB: {} BGP_NEIGHBOR keys".format(old_keys))
            assert len(old.calls) == 1 and payload in call["cmd"] and call["stdin"] is None
            assert call["rc"] == errno.E2BIG and old_keys == 0

            new = ShellRecorder(duthost)
            new_restore(new, asic_index, removed)
            call = new.calls[0]
            back, keys = read_neighbors(duthost, nsarg), count_keys(duthost, db_cli)
            print("\n================ NEW{} ================".format(label))
            print("$ " + call["cmd"])
            print("Payload:  {} entries, {} bytes on stdin".format(
                len(json.loads(call["stdin"])["BGP_NEIGHBOR"]), len(call["stdin"].encode())))
            print("Result:   rc={}".format(call["rc"]))
            print("ConfigDB: {} BGP_NEIGHBOR keys".format(keys))
            print("\nConfigDB BGP_NEIGHBOR == input JSON: {} ({}/{} entries)".format(back == removed, len(back), COUNT))
            assert call["cmd"] == "sudo sonic-cfggen {} -j /dev/stdin --write-to-db".format(nsarg)
            assert call["stdin"] == payload and call["rc"] == 0
            assert back == removed and len(back) == COUNT == keys
        finally:
            duthost.shell("sudo {0} CONFIG_DB keys 'BGP_NEIGHBOR|*' | xargs -r sudo {0} CONFIG_DB del".format(db_cli))
            duthost.shell("sudo sonic-cfggen {} -j {} --write-to-db".format(nsarg, snap_path))
            duthost.asic_instance(asic_index).reset_service("bgp")
            duthost.restart_service_on_asic("bgp", asic_index)
            bgp_up = wait_until(180, 10, 0, duthost.is_service_fully_started_per_asic_or_host, "bgp")
            duthost.shell("sudo rm -f {} {}".format(snap_path, scale_path))
            post_full = read_configdb(duthost, nsarg)
            print("Restored: full ConfigDB == pre-test snapshot: {}".format(post_full == pre_full))
        assert post_full == pre_full and bgp_up
```

The script is run in an Ansible inventory that already reaches the DUT and a sonic-mgmt Python environment with pytest-ansible. The test temporarily replaces the DUT's `BGP_NEIGHBOR` table and restarts `bgp`, then restores the original table in `finally`.

### Physical validation of `f03d4b593647c0115631393be546a01c78ffaf95`

Environment: Arista 720DT Broadcom leaf fanout on `SONiC.20231110.12`,
connected to a Nokia-7215 MX DUT on `SONiC.20260510.20`.

The public PR commits were cherry-picked into an isolated internal management
checkout. Validation exercised the existing cold config-reload, SWSS-container
wait and arp_update-stop tasks, followed by the exact changed Broadcom block.
It did not reprovision the shared root fanout or change the DUT image/configuration.

**Control reproduced the failure.** With the new readiness wait omitted, the
original FP reset ran before default trap creation completed:

```text
SAI_API_HOSTIF: field entry create failed with error Entry not found
SAI_HOSTIF_TRAP_ATTR_TRAP_TYPE: SAI_HOSTIF_TRAP_TYPE_TTL_ERROR
SAI_COMMON_API_CREATE: SAI_STATUS_ITEM_NOT_FOUND
orchagent: SIGABRT
```

Automatic service restart then left eight FP entries, no LLDP neighbors on the
two upstream DUT ports, and four established BGP sessions.

**Candidate validation passed:**

| Stage | Result |
|---|---|
| Initial patched smoke | 1/1 passed |
| Guarded repetitions | 5/5 passed |
| Separate final proof stage | 10/10 passed |

Across all 16 patched reloads:

- All 48 FP observations were empty, sampled after the reset sequence at
  approximately 0, 60 and 180 seconds.
- Both LLDP neighbors and all four BGP sessions recovered in every run and
  remained healthy at the final observation, beyond the 120-second LLDP TTL.
- The wait required two polls in 14 runs and one poll in two runs.
- The saved configuration hash did not change.
- No additional orchagent cores were created by the patched runs.

The original stopped arp_update state was restored after the campaign, and
the control-generated core was archived and removed. Final FP/LLDP/BGP health
was verified. The existing early arp_update-stop lifecycle was not changed by
this PR.

The isolated checks also passed: 20 shell scenarios, four real Ansible
retry/timeout/block-gating cases, five dispatcher/ASIC scope cases, and the
repository pre-commit hooks. A failed wait prevents both FP-reset commands.

This establishes the tested cold-reload behavior on the stated hardware/image;
it is not warm-restart validation or physical qualification of every Broadcom
SKU or the 202305 image.

Thanks @sakshamkhurana21, agreed on both. Addressed in d5db5bbe0f, and the PR description is updated to match.

**Multi-ASIC coverage**
- multi-asic-t1 now keeps its existing selection. When the dedup changes `t1_checker`, `get_test_scripts.py` also emits the original list as `multi-asic-t1-lag_checker`. The multi-asic job reads that key first and falls back to `t1_checker`, so baseline, manual and pre-defined `IMPACT_AREA_INFO` runs are unchanged.
- The job condition also accepts the new key. Otherwise a scoped PR whose t1 scripts are all deduped (e.g. only `tests/http` or `tests/radv`) would skip multi-asic entirely, including `http/test_http_copy.py` and `radv/test_radv_restart.py`.
- The dedup now only shortens t1-lag (338 → 300 on a full run). I'll evaluate the multi-asic removals in a separate PR.

**Enabled checkers**
- `INCLUDE_JOBS` is now passed from `pr_test_template.yml` through `get-impacted-area.yml` to `get_test_scripts.py --include-jobs`. A rule only applies if `INCLUDE_JOBS` enables a job that runs its `keep_in` checker, using the same `all`/`contains` check as `RUN_BY_INCLUDE_JOBS`. The checker-to-job map is `PR_CHECKER_JOBS` in `constant.py`.
- None of the PR pipelines I found hit this today: sonic-mgmt and sonic-buildimage `azure-pipelines.yml` and `docker-sonic-mgmt.yml` use `all`, and `docker-ptf.yml` includes `t0_job`. It's now enforced instead of assumed.

- `TestDedupIncludeJobs`: t1 keeps every script when `INCLUDE_JOBS` enables t1 but not t0, including lookalikes such as `t0_2vlans_job`. There's also a CLI test with the exact arguments the pipeline passes. These fail on the previous commit.
- `TestDedupKeepsMultiAsicT1`: the original t1 list is kept, including when the t1-lag list ends up empty.
- `TestPrCheckerJobs`: `PR_CHECKER_JOBS` matches the job conditions in `pr_test_template.yml`, and the multi-asic job reads its own key.

AI-assisted review, reviewed by Ying Xie (@yxieca).

Reviewed this against the merged Redfish HLD and the tests on `master`. The alignment work is good — 92 plan cases map 1:1 onto the 92 test functions in `tests/redfish/`, with no orphans in either direction. I would like to see it merged.

One thing to settle first, which I think is also the substance of the open thread above about removed Steps.

### Graceful Degradation is deleted, and nothing replaces it

The plan on `master` has **Section 10: Graceful Degradation**, two cases:

- Test Case #26 — Redfish works when Redis is temporarily unavailable (`test_redfish_degraded_redis_down`)
- Test Case #27 — Redfish works when FRU EEPROM is unreadable

These track a named HLD requirement. §5.2: *"Robust startup when some data sources (FRU, platform.json, Redis, `HOST_STATE`) are missing"*, expanded in §7.7: *"Missing sources degrade gracefully: inventory fields fall back per the precedence rules, firmware versions show `N/A`, no leak sensors means an empty `LeakDetectors` collection, an unavailable MAC keeps `Product=SONiCBMC`."*

This revision removes the section, and Open Item 1 states the intent is *"partly covered by the restart recovery tests (ObjectMapper re-registration) and by the telemetry bridge-unavailable test (bridge stopped)."*

Those two aren't substitutes. Restart recovery restarts a healthy bridge against a populated Redis; the telemetry case stops the bridge entirely. Neither runs the bridge against a *degraded data source*, which is what §7.7 specifies — and the four fallback behaviours it names (precedence fallback, `N/A` firmware, empty `LeakDetectors`, `Product=SONiCBMC`) end up with no case at all.

So the net effect on this requirement is 2 cases → 0.

### Suggestion

Either carry #26 and #27 forward into the new numbering, or keep Open Item 1 but state explicitly that §5.2/§7.7 robust-startup coverage is dropped and say what will cover it. Right now the Open Item reads as "already handled", which I do not think is accurate.

Worth noting the unit tests do cover part of it — `tests/unit-tests/inventory_model_test.cpp` in sonic-net/sonic-redfish has `DefaultsWhenAllSourcesAbsent` and the precedence suite. If the position is that degraded-source behaviour belongs at unit level rather than on hardware, that is a reasonable call; it just needs saying in the plan so the requirement is visibly accounted for rather than silently dropped.

### Separately

Three shipped HLD contracts have no case in this revision either — `409` on a full command queue, `Retry-After` on `503`, and the sub-second propagation latency in §5.2. Those predate this PR and I have filed them separately rather than asking you to grow this one: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/29009 and https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/29010

Thanks, @lolyu, for the detailed review and for pointing out #28531.

The core purpose of this change is to **make the test configuration take effect immediately**, rather than simply shorten a timeout. Replacing the policy file does not interrupt healthd's existing sleep: it reads the updated configuration at the next checking cycle. Restarting after installing the module policy avoids waiting out that previous sleep and starts the daemon with the intended test configuration. Restarting after restoration likewise applies the original policy promptly.

This behavior is generic. BMC's 300-second interval exposed the problem, but a shorter platform interval does not eliminate the delay between writing the configuration and the daemon consuming it. #28531 accommodates that delay by extending the process-exit test's wait on BMC; it does not make the newly installed policy effective immediately. The approaches are compatible and address different aspects of the problem.

For that reason, I would prefer to retain the generic scope rather than gate this fixture on `is_bmc()`. The two module-level restarts are deliberate: one applies the test policy, and the other applies the restored policy. Keeping a fast module baseline also means the existing per-test contexts restore to that baseline rather than repeatedly reintroducing a platform-dependent long polling interval. The restart overhead is a valid consideration, but this is not intended solely as a BMC runtime optimization, and we should not characterize the 600-to-180-second timeout-budget difference as a measured seven-minute saving.

I agree that the description should link #28531 and make this distinction clearer, and that refreshing the branch and revalidating with both changes present—including original-policy restoration—is appropriate. The existing Chipmunk results are historical; they are not validation of a refreshed branch. Representative non-BMC validation would also help assess the generic behavior and restart overhead.

## Verification on a Cisco 8102 (non-chassis, Q200/gb) T1 testbed: no regression found

**Setup**
- DUT: Cisco 8102-64H-O (HwSKU `Cisco-8102-C64`), single ASIC, topology `t1-64-lag`.
- Image: a SONiC 202605-based image with the Cisco 202605 SDK.
- `show platform npu global` on this DUT reports `HBM Absent` and `voq_allocation_mode : src_port_flow_hash`. It does not report `lossless_use_hbm`, `lossy_use_hbm` or `DRAM max packet descriptors in a pack`, so the generator logged `HBM usage: lossless=False, lossy=False` and took the SMS path.
- Code: a master-based branch (2026-11-04) with this PR's head `cd22e609f` applied. The patch applies cleanly.
- Command: `python3 -m pytest qos/test_qos_sai.py --topology t1,any ...`, with the same options as our nightly runs.
- Baseline: our nightly run of `qos/test_qos_sai.py` with the 202605 test code on the same DUT and image: 34 passed, 0 failed.

**Generated parameters**
On this DUT, the only parameter changes from this PR are:
- `lossy_queue_voq_3.packet_size` changes from 1350 to 64.
- `pg_drop` gets a new `cell_size: 384`.
- No `pkts_num_egr_mem` is generated for `topo-any`.

**Result: 35 passed with this PR**
- That covers every case that passes in the nightly baseline, plus `testQosSaiSeparatedDscpQueueMapping[single_asic-downstream]`. The baseline run skipped that case.
- Every case whose logic or generated parameters this PR changes passed.
- The one failure, `testQosSaiSeparatedDscpQueueMapping[single_asic-upstream]`, is intermittent and not related to this PR (note 2).

Runs:
1. This PR, unmodified: `testParameter` through `testQosSaiSharedReservationSize` passed (11 cases), and `testQosSaiHeadroomPoolWatermark` was XFAIL. `testQosSaiBufferPoolWatermark` failed (note 1), so I stopped the run there.
2. This PR, with `permit_only_test_traffic_on_fanout` removed from the four tests listed in note 1, on the remaining cases: 24 passed, 1 failed (note 2), 210 skipped.
3. A/B run of the same branch without this PR, on the two cases that failed: `testQosSaiBufferPoolWatermark[single_asic-wm_buf_pool_lossless]` failed the same way (note 1), and `testQosSaiSeparatedDscpQueueMapping[single_asic-upstream]` passed.

**Notes: failures not caused by this PR**
1. **`permit_only_test_traffic_on_fanout` takes the DUT's LAGs down.**
   - On master, this fixture also guards `testQosSaiBufferPoolWatermark`, `testQosSaiLossyQueueVoq`, `testQosSaiDscpQueueMapping` and `testQosSaiDscpToPgMapping`. On 202605 it only guards the two headroom-pool tests.
   - On this T1 LAG testbed, the fixture's `supervisorctl stop lacpd` returns rc=1, because the teamd container has no `lacpd` program. The fixture still applies the EOS fanout egress MAC ACL that drops LACP.
   - The DUT PortChannels then go down, and the PTF probe in `get_multiple_flows` fails with `Expected packet was not received`.
   - The same branch without this PR fails identically. #28009 addresses this.
   - To verify this PR's changes, I removed the fixture from those four tests locally, as on 202605.
2. **`testQosSaiSeparatedDscpQueueMapping[single_asic-upstream]` is intermittent.**
   - It failed in both runs with this PR and passed in the A/B run without it.
   - In the failures, the per-queue deltas were `[1, 33, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0]`, so only 38 of the 64 packets were counted. The log showed `Queue counters updated successfully after 0.02 seconds (1 iterations)`.
   - The cause: without `tc_to_dscp_count_map`, `check_all_expected_counters_updated` returns as soon as any queue counter changes, so the counters can be read before all packets are counted.
   - This PR doesn't touch that test or `DscpMappingPB`.

**Not covered by this verification:**
- The T2 chassis/HBM paths: HBM geometry and cross-ASIC egress memory.
- Cisco 8111 (gr), 8122 (gr2) and Q100 (pac).
- Images with pre-202605 Cisco SDKs.

Update at 5cb1b63ed, following the teardown errors reported in the previous regression on the 32-neighbor NH-5010-F-O64.

Root cause of those errors: the single remove patch deleted the peer's BGP rows and its interface together, so orchagent tried to delete the peer's next hop while routes in the 16-way ECMP groups still referenced it (`SAI_STATUS_OBJECT_IN_USE`, retried until the routes drained). The flow now removes the peer in stages (`remove_peer_via_gcu`): BGP peering first, then the interface / QoS / port rows once bgpd has dropped the peer and the prefixes have left the RIB, then the base rows. That is also the order an operator would use to drain a peer. The remove and re-add assertions are unchanged.

Test-only fix in `tests/dualtor/test_orchagent_active_tor_downstream.py`. Two-line change, self-restore restricted to IPv4 plus an `lladdr` guard on the final cleanup. Verified against the real code; no functional issues found. CI is 20/20 green.

**Verified**
- The `KeyError: 'lladdr'` claim is real. `flush_neighbor()` restores with `neighbor_details['lladdr']` unconditionally when `restore=True` — `tests/common/dualtor/dual_tor_utils.py:1368-1369`. If the captured neighbor has no link-layer address, that indexing raises `KeyError`.
- `get_neighbor()` only extracts `dev` and `lladdr` via regex and returns a dict that omits `lladdr` when the `ip neighbor show` line has none — `tests/common/dualtor/dual_tor_utils.py:1352`. This matches the reported `{'dev': 'Vlan1000'}` capture for the IPv6 neighbor, confirming the failure path.
- The two edits correctly close both restore paths named in the description:
  - `restore=ip_version == "ipv4"` (line 83) stops `flush_neighbor` self-restore for IPv6, so its `finally` no longer touches `lladdr`.
  - `if removed_neighbor and removed_neighbor.get("lladdr")` (line 135) guards the explicit final restore.
- No regression for the has-`lladdr` case: when the IPv6 neighbor was reachable, `removed_neighbor` still contains `lladdr`, the guard passes and the final block restores it (lines 135-142) — i.e. the restore simply moves from `flush_neighbor` to the test's own `finally`. IPv4 is statically configured and always carries `lladdr`, so its behavior is unchanged.
- Recovery for the no-`lladdr` IPv6 case does not depend on the skipped restore: `remove_neighbor`'s `finally` runs `supervisorctl restart arp_update` (line 93) and the test then waits up to 60s for the entry to become reachable (line 123). Skipping a restore that could never have succeeded is the correct behavior.

**Nits**
- Testing was `py_compile` only, which is expected for a testbed-dependent dualtor test; the change is small and the logic is verified above.

## Review: sonic-mgmt#27189

Overall this is a well-reasoned fix, with excellent hardware validation data in the description. Went through `pfc_storm.py` and `pfc_gen_brcm_xgs.py` in detail.

### Things that look solid
- `BCM_CHIP_NAMES` resolution with HwSKU-table fallback (ASIC → HwSKU → `None`) is a sensible widening, and the DNX/TH4-and-older omissions are well justified in the description.
- `endAllPfcStorm()` now clears backpressure on *all* interfaces before doing the slower per-interface config restore — this is a real, well-evidenced fix for the restore-time spread (`~3.4s/port` → `~0.5s/port`).
- `_restorePfcConfig()`/`startPfcStorm()` now agree on which priorities to touch (`(1 << prio) & self.priority`), so stopping no longer clobbers unrelated lossless priorities — good catch.
- `SignalCleanup` now also handles `SIGINT`, and the `try/finally: fs.endAllPfcStorm()` in `main()` is safe against the double-invocation from `sigHandler()`'s `sys.exit(0)` because `endAllPfcStorm()` is explicitly idempotent (`intfs, self.intfsEnabled = self.intfsEnabled, []`).
- Moving the `frontPanelIntfFromKernelIntfName` EOS conversion out of the per-interface loop so it also applies to `clearStalePfcBackpressure(interfaces)` is correct and needed.

### One asymmetry worth a closer look

`start_storm()` calls `self._ensure_pfc_gen_deployed()` before `_prepare_start_template()`, but `stop_storm()` does not call it before `_prepare_stop_template()`:

```python
def start_storm(self):
    self._ensure_pfc_gen_deployed()
    self._prepare_start_template()
    ...

def stop_storm(self):
    self._prepare_stop_template()   # no _ensure_pfc_gen_deployed() here
    ...
```

Both `_prepare_start_template()` and `_prepare_stop_template()` branch on `self.pfc_gen_chip_name` to decide between the t2 template and the arista/XGS template, and the arista stop templates (`pfc_storm_stop_arista_*.j2`) bake `pfc_gen_chip_name` into the `pkill -f '...'` pattern used to find and signal the running generator. If `pfc_gen_chip_name`/`fanout_asic_type` on the instance ever get out of sync with what was actually deployed for the *current* `peer_info` when `stop_storm()` runs (e.g. some future caller does `update_peer_info()` then `stop_storm()` without an intervening `start_storm()`/`deploy_pfc_gen()` on the new peer), `_prepare_stop_template()` could render a `pkill -f` pattern that doesn't match the actually-running process — silently failing to stop the storm.

I checked the current callers (`test_pfcwd_function.py`, `test_pfcwd_cli.py`, `qos/test_pfc_pause.py`, `PFCMultiStorm`) and in every path today `start_storm()` (or an explicit `deploy_pfc_gen()`) is called for a peer before `stop_storm()` is called for that same peer, so this doesn't currently manifest. But given this PR already had to fix a very similar staleness bug for `start_storm()` (item 5 in the description), it seems worth the same defensive fix for symmetry/future-proofing:

```python
def stop_storm(self):
    self._ensure_pfc_gen_deployed()
    self._prepare_stop_template()
    ...
```

Not blocking given current call sites and the strong hardware test evidence, but flagging since a silent "storm never actually stopped" failure mode would be exactly the kind of flaky/misleading test result this PR is trying to eliminate.

Reviewed (multi-model + SME, ground-validated against fwutil source). Well-structured 5-case plan — no blocking issues. Two accuracy points worth correcting before implementation:

1. **TC3 version-policy verb/semantics.** `--force`/`-f` is an option on `fwutil update fw` only (main.py:303), not on `install` — `install fw` has no `--force` and no version check (`install_fw()` → `component.install_firmware(path)` directly, main.py:212). The refuse-same/refuse-older/force-downgrade matrix is generic only for `update` (`is_firmware_update_required(...) or force`, main.py:337); there is no generic newer-vs-older comparison in fwutil core — downgrade refusal is vendor `install_firmware` behavior. Suggest rewriting TC3 around `fwutil update ... -f` for the force path, and scoping the same/older policy to `update` semantics (or explicitly to vendor behavior, marked platform-dependent).
2. **TC5 techsupport firmware-version capture.** `generate_dump` collects `show platform syseeprom/psustatus/ssdhealth/temperature/fan` + `show platform versions`, but no `fwutil show status` / `show platform firmware`. So "techsupport captures the BMC firmware version" is not true today unless it surfaces in `show platform versions`. Suggest scoping TC5 to what the dump actually collects, or making dump-extension (`fwutil show status`) a requirement.

Minor nits: `install` examples omit `-y` for non-interactive automation; "never left in an unusable state" is a platform contract not a fwutil guarantee; anchor the expected `fwutil` syslog pattern for a deterministic scrape; specify what "mismatched device" means (metadata/platform-key). `tests/platform_tests/fwutil/` is the right home and already parametrizes components.

— Reviewed by Ying (AI-assisted review)

**`get_portchannel_changetime()` — does this now silently swallow real CLI/parse failures on PortChannel topologies?**

Both call sites are already guarded by `if self.has_dut_portchannels:` (lines ~172 and ~218), and `check_change_time` is only invoked in the `has_dut_portchannels` branch. So on an isolated topology the function is never called — the empty/no-PortChannel case is handled entirely by the caller-side gate.

That means every `return None` inside `get_portchannel_changetime()` only fires on a topology that *does* have PortChannels, where `show interfaces po1 | json` is expected to return real data:

```python
def get_portchannel_changetime(self):
    portchannel_output = self.do_cmd("show interfaces po1 | json")
    portchannel_output = "\n".join(portchannel_output.split("\r\n")[1:-1])
    if not portchannel_output.strip():
        return None                      # empty CLI output
    try:
        po_info = json.loads(portchannel_output, strict=False)
        return po_info['interfaces']['Port-Channel1']['lastStatusChangeTimestamp']
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError) as err:
        self.log('Failed to parse Port-Channel1 status: {}'.format(err))
        return None                      # parse / lookup failure

Now it's caught and returns `None`, which flows into `sample["po_changetime"]` and then `check_change_time`. `None != timestamp` compares without raising, so the run continues — but a genuine CLI or script failure on a PortChannel topology is now masked (only a log line, no test failure), and could contribute a spurious state-change count.
